frontier.hypothesis: Reuse the `limit`-holding pseudo (or a variable that would occupy the same storage) for a second, USED, loop-VARIANT value near the `i < limit` compare, so the pseudo becomes multi-set and loop.c's invariant-motion no longer treats it as a movable -- this is the [[defeat-licm-hoist-var-reuse]] mechanism applied to the loop BOUND rather than the table INDEX (which is what all four 'share i*2' probes, now killed on three chassis generations, actually tested).
frontier.mechanism: loop.c's strength_reduce / find_and_verify_loops only treats a pseudo as a movable invariant if it has exactly one set reaching every use inside the loop; a genuinely multi-set pseudo is excluded from the movable-pseudo set and is not hoisted-then-spilled the same way.
frontier.next_probe: Identify a loop-variant value computed near the `limit` use (the `i < limit` compare site, or immediately before/after it) that could plausibly share ONE C variable with `limit` under a truthful semantic reading (not an invented alias) -- e.g. restructuring the loop guard/increment so the same local is legitimately reassigned inside the loop body. If no truthful reuse candidate exists, this lever may not be reachable without inventing a value, in which case the next forensics step is a fresh `.lreg`/`.rtl` dump specifically of the post-spill reload sequence to see what ELSE conflicts with reg 11 in the loop body (the conflict list at line ~14790-14810 of text1b.greg, not yet cross-referenced against source-level candidates).

frontier.hypothesis: Re-attempt the outer 0..1-counter loop restructuring (`for (n = 0; n < 2; n++) { i = start + n; ... }`) with a correctly brace-balanced splice -- this session's attempt was a tooling artifact (build_insns=8, syntax error), not a real measurement, so this C shape is genuinely untried.
frontier.mechanism: Decoupling the loop-carried `i` (used for both indexing and the bound compare) from a fresh, single-purpose counter `n` might change which pseudo global_alloc treats as the loop-invariant/loop-variant split, potentially avoiding the reg-11 spill path entirely by giving the bound test a trivially-constant (`n < 2`) comparison instead of a computed `limit`.
frontier.next_probe: Rewrite tmp/grind/func_80056CB8/s51/splice_ncount.py by hand (not via blind string-replace) to preserve brace balance and the full loop body, then measure via sandbox --disable all.
